activity_text: Anti-Gram+ & Gram-, Antifungal, candidacidal, Anti-MRSA, Anti-inflammatory, anti-sepsis
comments_text: Peptide discovery: Found in multiple species. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is most similar (80%) to Brevinin-1GHa. Activity: Active against S. aureus or MRSA (MIC 2-4 uM), E. coli (MIC 8 uM), P. aeruginosa (MIC 32 uM), C. albicans (MIC 4 uM). It binds LPS and shows anti-inflammatory effects by suppressing the release of TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, and IL-6 from mouse RAW 264.7 cells ( Tian et al., 2023. Structure: the peptide is random coiled in water and became helical in complex with SDS, LPS, or SDS+LPS. Animal model:mouse: inflammation model (acute edema) was established with carrageenan administration. IP injection of the peptide alleviated the swelling of the right paw of mice, thereby showing the anti-inflammatory effect in vivo as well. Replaced with a more active peptide 5/2020; formatted 4/2024; 8/2024
title: Brevinin-1GHd, A Novel Hylarana Guentheri Skin Secretion-Derived Brevinin-1 Type Peptide With Antimicrobial and Anticancer Therapeutic Potential

comments_text: Comment: Brevinin-1GHd with its excellent antimicrobial and anticancer activities is a promising candidate for a novel antibiotic agent, and study of its structure activity relationships also provided a rational template for further research and peptide analog design. In the reference, the example of Brevinin-1GHd is used to challenge the importance of "Rana-Box", which appears in many AMPs originating from frogs and contains an intermolecular disulfide bridge at the C-terminus of the peptide and seven to nine amino acid residues.
cytotoxicity_text: [Ref.32347293]Brevinin-1GHd showed significant cytotoxicity toward human HMEC-1 and HaCaT cells at concentrations of 0.00001 and 0.0001 M, respectively. Brevinin-1GHd induced one cell viability of 56% on HMEC-1 and the other cell viability of 75% on HaCat.
hemolytic_activity_text: [Ref.32347293] Brevinin-1GHd displayed 13% hemolysis on horse red blood cells at its highest MIC/MBC value of the tested bacteria P. aeruginosa (32 ?M). However, when the concentration increased above 64 μM, the hemolytic activity of Brevinin-1GHd also gradually increased. At the concentration of 64, 128, 256 and 512 μM, it displayed about 36%, 64%, 83% and 108% hemolysis.
target_organism_text: [Ref.32347293] Gram-positive bacteria: S. aureus (MIC = 2 μM/MBC= 4 ?M), MRSA(MIC = 4 μM/MBC = 4?M); ##Gram-negative: E. coli(MIC = 8 μM/MBC = 8 ?M), P. aeruginosa(MIC = 32 μM/MBC = 32?M); ##Fungi: C. albicans(MIC = 4 μM/MBC = 8?M）
